The combat in the second installment of the series is deep. Yes, it is way slower than the third installment and even slower than the first. The movement also feels more floaty and the weapon impacts have no real weight. However, the level of control on your actions is still here.


There are a lot of weapons, some of them have the same moves and different looks/range/stats only. That said, there is a lot of weapon variety still, and you have tons of options depending on your build. 

Powerstance is also a cool feature, which allows you to use different weapon combinations to use dual attacks with L1 and L2 (you'll need high stats though).


That said, the game is awesome. It has tons of content, a lot of variety in levels and bosses (though level design is a step back from the other games), lots of weapons, viable magic/sorceries/pyro/faith (though faith is mostly for buffs in this game). 

There are a lot of bosses (31 in vanilla, 40 with the dlcs), most of the vanilla ones are forgettable though (most have cool concepts I think). 

The dlcs and their bosses are meant for end-game, way harder than vanilla, and are among the best content in all Souls-games in my opinion, with awesome bossfights.

Overall, if you can get over worse level design/world design, less memorable vanilla bosses, and a different and slightly slower gameplay, then you'll enjoy it a lot, it has tons of replayability (and a great pvp as well).

Be sure to play the game on a modern console or PC to get the best experience. You get hit during your rolls because you don't have a lot of i-frames to start with in this game. Leveling up your adaptability will allow you to have more i-frames (around 25-30 adp is recommended for most builds), and to use heal items slightly quicker as well.

The movement is more floaty, but it is still precise, you'll get used to it with time.

Estus isn't really meant to be used in a combat situation with enemies close to you. Lifegems are what you should use most of the time, they are unlimited and quick to use.

Taking a hit will stagger you depending on the attack, the poise you have and if you're in hyper-frames (attacking with an ultra-weapon) or not. When this happens, roll the hell away.

The inspirations aren't really an issue to be honest. I think it's cool.

**Darkend:** A new island to explore with its own enemies and lore, heavily inspired by Souls games. It's cool, though it lacked directions the last time I played it (I did not realize I had finished it all). It should have more content now too, though I don't know if it's good or not.

**Clockwork Castle:** A new house and a quest to go with it in some new levels. The most atmospheric and immersive part of the game for me. The story is great and everything feels surreal but makes sense. It feels slightly too long though.  


**The Forgotten City:** You all know that one. A new city to explore with its own story and lore and a cool twist. That said, a lot of the content is optional and if you guess what you have to do for the main quest you can skip all the optional stuff without wanting to. Also, in side-quests it can be difficult to guess what you're supposed to do.
